item.title: Tree is damaged problem, 30th October
item.description:
I live at 31 Roman Hackle Avenue, GL50 4RF. Between my house and no. 29, there's overgrown holly trees that are knocking against our house when it's windy. Photos are attached of where the treea are located and how far they reach. Because there are squirrels in the larger Elm tree (images also attached), we are concerned that they could use the holly trees to reach our roof/loft. Can you please advise whether these trees are the responsibility of our neighbour or not? He is an elderly gentleman who said he wasn't able to get clarity. Could someone have a look in person? He believes the trees are on the council side of the hedge but I don't know if that's correct. We are wanting to know 2 things regarding those holly trees: 1. Will the council cut these trees back? 2. If not, how can we do this ourselves with the access needing to be blocked for safety whilst cutting. The Elm is breaking up the pathway with it's roots. I'm very concerned that this also needs to be cut back because of the risk to our garden. The image of the broken pathway (which I assume is your responsibility) doesn't show just how the extent of the damage, or two raised parts of the path are. Who has responsibility for cutting that tree back? Should the home owners be the ones to control this? Any help you can give would be much appreciated.
Report on FixMyStreet

item.title: Dangerous trees leaning onto property, 30th October
item.description:
Footpath behind 23, Merestones Drive, Cheltenham, GL50 2SU. Two of the trees are leaning over the path, one quite substantially and with the frequent high winds it became clear that it won't take much for it to destroy the fence as the branches are leaning heavily over the back of the property and into the garden. Please could someone come and see the tree and remove the dangerous branches to protect the rest of the tree and the property. Thank you.
